- **Customer concentration and non-renewal:** 61% of revenue comes from two big-box retail customers, and one of them has not renewed its contract, which expires in Q1. Losing it would remove a large share of revenue.
- **Credit covenant breach risk:** The $20M revolving credit line renews in December and requires gross margin above 36%, while margin has already fallen to 38% from 42%. Further erosion could breach the covenant and jeopardize financing.
- **Margin pressure from input costs:** Gross margin dropped four points, to 38% from 42%, as steel input costs rose 15%. Continued cost increases would deepen the squeeze on profitability.
- **Competitive price pressure:** A rival cut prices 10% in our core category in August, threatening volume or forcing us to cut prices and lower margins further.
- **Revenue shortfall and operational execution:** Revenue of $41.2M missed the $43M plan, inventory rose to 140 days on hand, and the ERP migration is 4 months late and $1.1M over budget. These point to weak demand visibility, tied-up working capital, and cost and project-control problems.

I'm reviewing a quarterly report and need the main risks pulled out of the summary pasted below this prompt. The list will be read as-is, so it has to be self-contained and use no outside names.

Read the summary and list the top risks to the business, most significant first. Reply with exactly 5 bullet points. Make each bullet one or two sentences that state the risk and the evidence for it from the summary. Where the summary gives a figure, include it. Refer to competitors only in general terms, such as "a rival" or "competing offerings", and never by name, because this list will be shared outside the company. Reply with the 5 bullets only. Add no introduction, closing remarks, or extra bullets.

Q3 summary, Northwind Tools
Revenue $41.2M (+6% QoQ), below the $43M plan. Gross margin fell to 38% from 42% as steel input costs rose 15%. 61% of revenue comes from two big-box retail customers; one of them, HomeMax, has not renewed its contract, which expires in Q1. Inventory rose to 140 days on hand. Acme Fastening cut prices 10% in our core category in August. The ERP migration is 4 months late and $1.1M over budget. Headcount is flat. A $20M revolving credit line renews in December; the covenant requires margin above 36%.
